items.title: Hipparchs Himmelsglobus
items.note: Reconstructs the celestial globe implied by Hipparchus's Commentary on Aratus and compares its star data with the Almagest catalogue and Babylonian astrometry.

items.title: On the making of Ptolemy's star catalog
items.venue: Archive for History of Exact Sciences
items.note: Statistical and adjustment analysis of the Almagest coordinates aimed at reconstructing how the catalogue was compiled and what share rests on earlier data.

items.title: Accuracy of magnitudes in pre-telescopic star catalogs
items.who: P. Protte and S. M. Hoffmann
items.note: Converts Ptolemy's, al-Sufi's and Tycho's magnitudes to the V scale and compares them with Hipparcos, giving an independent error profile for the Almagest data.

items.title: The determination of Hipparchus' phenomena and their consistency with the Almagest star catalog
items.note: Tests whether the risings and settings in Hipparchus's Commentary can be derived from a globe built on Almagest-based coordinates, finding most of them consistent.

items.title: Anatomical identifications of stars: Textual descriptions in Ptolemy's star catalogue
items.venue: Studies in History and Philosophy of Science
items.note: Quantifies the formulaic language of more than 700 anatomical star descriptions in the catalogue, a textual layer relevant to how the catalogue was composed.

items.title: New evidence for Hipparchus' Star Catalogue revealed by multispectral imaging
items.who: V. Gysembergh, P. J. Williams and E. Zingg
items.venue: Journal for the History of Astronomy
items.note: Recovers equatorial star coordinates for Corona Borealis from the Codex Climaci Rescriptus undertext, attributes them to Hipparchus and dates them to about 129 BCE.

items.title: Newly discovered illustrated texts of Aratus and Eratosthenes within Codex Climaci Rescriptus
items.who: P. J. Williams, P. James, J. Klair and P. Malik
items.note: Describes the wider Greek astronomical undertext of the palimpsest that carries the putative Hipparchan coordinates, establishing its codicological context.

items.title: Gaia Data Release 3
items.note: Current proper motions and positions used as the modern reference when dating ancient catalogue coordinates by precession and proper motion.

items.title: An astronomical analysis of the data in the pseudo-Hipparchus palimpsest in the Codex Climaci Rescriptus
items.who: G. Graßhoff and S. M. Hoffmann
items.venue: Journal for the History of Astronomy
items.note: Disputes the 2022 dating and argues that the palimpsest's terminology and data format do not match Hipparchus, so it cannot settle the Ptolemy question.

items.title: Un contributo al dibattito sui rapporti tra i cataloghi stellari di Tolomeo e Ipparco
items.note: Preprint arguing from the different observing latitudes of the two astronomers against the originality of the Ptolemaic catalogue.

items.title: A note on the new evidence for Hipparchus' star catalogue
items.who: V. Gysembergh, P. Williams and E. Zingg
items.venue: Journal for the History of Astronomy
items.note: Reply to Graßhoff and Hoffmann reaffirming the Hipparchan attribution and adducing support from P. Aberdeen 12.

items.title: Hipparchus' Star Catalogues
items.venue: Archive for History of Exact Sciences
items.note: Weighs the Codex Climaci Rescriptus fragment, the Aratus Latinus and P. Aberdeen 12 against Hipparchus's surviving Commentary to assess what they show about his catalogue.

items.title: Synchrotron X-ray fluorescence imaging of the Codex Climaci Rescriptus at SLAC
items.who: V. Gysembergh, U. Bergmann, S. Webb et al.
items.venue: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory (reported in Scientific American)
items.note: X-ray fluorescence scanning separated the calcium-rich Greek undertext from later iron-gall ink, recovering further coordinates; full results remain unpublished.

items.title: Speed-Error Cross-Correlation Dating of Ancient Star Catalogues, with Application to the Almagest
items.note: Unreviewed preprint with released code proposing a proper-motion dating method validated on Tycho and Ulugh Beg, then applied to the Almagest.

items.title: The Astronomy of Hipparchus
items.note: Translates and analyses the Commentary on Aratus and reconstructs Hipparchus's lost star catalogue using a modern precession model.

items.title: Spica and the ancient astronomers: on Hipparchus's longitude of Spica and the date of Timocharis's lunar eclipse
items.venue: Archive for History of Exact Sciences
items.note: Re-examines Hipparchus's longitude of Spica, the datum behind his precession estimate and thus behind any epoch shift between the two catalogues.
